column2: WARNING CEMS Heated Sample Line Sign – Tubing Under Jacket Can Burn – 8x12 Aluminum
column3:
Tubing Under Jacket Can Burn. This WARNING CEMS Heated Sample Line sign from CGAP Safety reads: CEMS HEATED SAMPLE LINE / TUBING UNDER JACKET CAN BURN / ISOLATE LINE HEAT AND COOL / BEFORE OPENING THE BUNDLE. Written for power plants, cement kilns, industrial boiler plants.

Why this sign matters

The sample tubing is held at high temperature by heat trace inside the insulated jacket, so cutting or opening the bundle exposes tubing hot enough to cause serious burns.

Where to post it

On the sample line support or junction box where the insulated bundle is opened for service.

Who orders it

Plant instrument and CEMS technicians.

Rust-resistant .065 aluminum, UV-resistant print, pre-drilled in all four corners. Made in the USA. Related standards to review for your site: OSHA 1910.147; OSHA 1910.132; ANSI Z535.2. A sign supports your safety program; it does not replace guarding, lockout or training.

column2: WARNING Turbine Turning Gear Sign – Gear Can Auto Engage And Roll The Shaft – 8x12 Aluminum
column3:

This WARNING Turbine Turning Gear sign from CGAP Safety reads: TURBINE TURNING GEAR / GEAR CAN AUTO ENGAGE AND ROLL / THE SHAFT WITHOUT WARNING / LOCK OUT BEFORE HAND BARRING. Why this sign matters

The turning gear can engage on its own as the turbine coasts down and roll the shaft with high torque, catching hands or a barring tool in the gear mesh.

On the turning gear enclosure or bearing pedestal next to the engagement lever and hand barring point.

Turbine maintenance supervisors and plant mechanics.

column3:
Photocell Off Is Not Power Off. This WARNING High Mast Light Pole Base sign from CGAP Safety reads: HIGH MAST LIGHT SERVICE POWER / PHOTOCELL OFF IS NOT POWER OFF / FEED IN BASE CAN STILL SHOCK / LOCK OUT AND TEST BEFORE WORK. Written for municipal electric departments, highway lighting crews, ports and rail yards.

Why this sign matters

Lights turned off by a photocell or timer still have a live feed in the pole base, so a worker who trusts dark lights can contact energized conductors.

On the high mast pole base door, at eye level above the handhole.

Who orders it

Municipal electric line crews and lighting technicians.
